instruction_problems: CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS is missing. Claude Code 2.1.319 always sends max_tokens=32000 and keeps min(max_output,20000) of CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS free for output. The printed setup works at this trial's 90112 (effectiveWindow 70112) and the bridge's 65536 (45536). At 32768 the effective window is 12768, below the ~12k base prompt, so it compacts on turn 1. At 16384 Claude Code refuses ('Prompt is too long', exit 1). cyrlm can print contexts under ~45k for smaller machines, and its claude-code MinContext (33000+8192=41192) does not include this reserve.

The Note on CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER=0 is inaccurate for 2.1.319. Without it Claude Code prepends a system block 'x-anthropic-billing-header: cc_version=2.1.319.<hash>; cc_entrypoint=sdk-cli;'. The block is identical across requests within a session but changes between sessions/prompts (.882 vs .bae observed). So =0 is what lets new sessions and subagents reuse the cached prefix. It is still right to set; cyrlm detected and explained the resulting miss correctly (#25: miss at token 1).

CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1 is missing. Without it Claude Code calls Anthropic for a Bootstrap fetch, GrowthBook flags and a metrics opt-out / BigQuery telemetry export (they failed here, with no visible effect or slowdown). With it the debug log shows '[Bootstrap] Skipped: Nonessential traffic disabled' and no telemetry errors. Without it, cyrlm's Privacy line ('only model requests leave it') is untrue for the harness itself, and an offline machine makes failing calls.

No headless/automation form is printed. `claude -p` with no stdin redirect waits 3 s and prints 'Warning: no stdin data received in 3s'. A working non-interactive run needs `-p '<task>' --allowedTools Bash --permission-mode acceptEdits < /dev/null`.

The scenario line says 'Claude Code — 33k-token system prompt + tools'. Measured with 2.1.319 (cyrlm's own token counts in message_start): 10.6k in -p mode (12 tools), 12.0k interactive (13 tools), 19.9k with ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=false (22 tools). FIRST REPLY (14 s), TASK time and MinContext are therefore based on a prompt about 2.7x too large.

The printed command assumes `claude` is on PATH. After `npm i @anthropic-ai/claude-code` without -g the binary is ./node_modules/.bin/claude, and FindBinary only checks ~/.claude/local/claude and ~/.local/bin/claude.

request_shape_notes: Endpoints: `HEAD /api/hello` once at startup (a fire-and-forget preconnect whose response is ignored; cyrlm returns 404, harmless), then `POST /v1/messages?beta=true` with stream:true always. No count_tokens or /v1/models calls in -p or interactive mode.

Headers: Authorization: Bearer cyrlm; anthropic-version: 2023-06-01; anthropic-beta: claude-code-20250219, interleaved-thinking-2025-05-14, context-management-2025-06-27, mid-conversation-tool-changes-2026-07-01, thinking-token-count-2026-05-13, advanced-tool-use-2025-11-20, effort-2025-11-24; X-Claude-Code-Session-Id; x-app: cli; anthropic-dangerous-direct-browser-access: true; User-Agent: claude-cli/2.1.319 (external, sdk-cli). Request body ~46 KB.

Body fields: model, max_tokens=32000, stream, thinking={type:'adaptive', display:'omitted'} (-p) or 'updates' (stream-json/interactive), output_config={effort:'high'}, context_management={edits:[{type:'clear_thinking_20251015', keep:'all'}]}, metadata.user_id (a JSON string with device_id/session_id). cyrlm maps effort to reasoning_effort:'high' upstream and correctly ignores context_management and metadata.

system is an array of text blocks with cache_control: an optional billing-header block (absent with CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER=0); 'You are a Claude agent, built on Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK.' (-p) or 'You are Claude Code, Anthropic's official CLI for Claude.' (interactive); then the main prompt (~5.7–5.9k chars). cyrlm joins these into one leading system message.

New in this version: a role:'system' message inside messages[], right after the first user turn ('# Environment ...', with cache_control). cyrlm handles it correctly: NormalizeForTemplates appends it to the user turn as '[System note]...', keeping one leading system message and a stable prefix. No strict-template 500s occurred.

The first user turn is two text blocks (a <\system-reminder> with attribution and skill listing, then the task). cyrlm flattens these into a string. tool_result blocks carry cache_control and is_error (ignored/handled correctly). Assistant history replays thinking blocks with cyrlm's signature 'cyrlm-simulated', which Claude Code accepts.

Tools: 12 (-p) or 13 (interactive) custom tools with no `type` field (Agent, Bash, Edit, ListAgents, Read, ReportFindings, ScheduleWakeup, Skill, ToolSearch, Workflow, DeferredToolPlaceholder, Write). Tool search is on by default even with a third-party base URL ('[ToolSearch:optimistic] ... result=true'), so the model must call ToolSearch to get WebFetch, WebSearch, NotebookEdit, Cron*, etc. Glob and Grep are not available in this build. DeferredToolPlaceholder has defer_loading:true and the description 'never call this tool'; cyrlm forwards it upstream as an ordinary function.

Deferred-tool flow: the ToolSearch tool_result content is [{type:'tool_reference', tool_name:'WebFetch'}]. The next request adds WebFetch with defer_loading:true, inserted alphabetically mid-list (before Workflow). cyrlm DROPS the tool_reference and sends the upstream tool message as content '' (the model sees an empty search result). In try/serve this is silent: no '!' line in trial.log. Only bridge mode logs '! ignored tool_reference block in tool_result'.

The mid-list insertion changes the rendered tool block, so on a local runtime it invalidates the prompt cache from that point. cyrlm's simulator caught it (miss at token 8663) but labeled it 'a different conversation replaced this one in the cache'.

A side request in interactive mode generates the session title: no tools, 678 tokens, output_config={effort:'high', format:{type:'json_schema', schema:{title:string}}}. cyrlm silently drops output_config.format (no response_format upstream) and still sends reasoning_effort:'high' for it.

Assistant thinking text is decoded into msg.Reasoning but never sent upstream: upstream.go BuildBody emits assistant content:null plus tool_calls only, with no reasoning_content. Interleaved reasoning across a tool-call chain is lost (this matters for Qwen3.x / gpt-oss templates).

Usage: message_start reports cyrlm's local token count (e.g. input_tokens 10555, cache_read 0); message_delta reports the upstream count with the simulated cache split (input 1, cache_read 99). This is fine with a real upstream, but message_start should already carry the cache split. The fake's constant prompt_tokens=100 is why trial.log shows 'prompt 100' on some lines; that is a fake artifact.

Prompt cache: CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER=0 gives a byte-identical system prefix across sessions. Session summary: 97% of 34.6k prompt tokens reused, 8 misses (mostly cross-session or tool changes in my tests).

Add a Note: 'Claude Code keeps up to 20k tokens of the window free for its reply; cyrlm lowers that so a <64k local context does not compact on every turn.'

Add {"CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC","1"} (at least when Tuned), with a Note that it stops Claude Code's own telemetry, bootstrap and update calls to Anthropic, so only model requests leave the machine. Reword the attribution Note to: 'CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER=0 removes a per-session attribution line at the start of the system prompt, so new sessions and subagents reuse the cached prompt.'

Add a Note with the non-interactive form: `claude -p "<task>" --permission-mode acceptEdits --allowedTools Bash < /dev/null` (without the stdin redirect it waits 3 s for stdin). Optionally add node_modules/.bin/claude and the npm global prefix to knownBinaries["claude"].

Change claude-code BasePromptTokens from 33000 to ~12000. Measured with 2.1.319 and tool search on: 10.6k in -p, 12.0k interactive; 19.9k with ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=false; users with MCP servers or CLAUDE.md will be higher. Set an explicit MinContext of about base + output reserve + ~13k autocompact buffer: ~45056 with the default 20k reserve, or ~36864 if SetupFor sets CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=8192. Update the 'Scenario: Claude Code — 33k-token system prompt' text to match.

Handle tool_result parts of type "tool_reference" instead of warning and dropping them: append text such as "Tool loaded: <tool_name> (its schema is now in your tool list; call it directly)." so the local model does not see an empty ToolSearch result.

Parse `defer_loading`. Drop deferred tools that no tool_reference in the conversation has loaded; in practice that is DeferredToolPlaceholder, which says 'never call this tool' and only wastes tokens or invites a small model to call it. Optionally move loaded deferred tools to the end of the tool list, in the order they were first referenced, so loading one disturbs less of the rendered prefix.

Print req.Warnings ('#n anthropic  ! <msg>') in the try/serve path as well. Today only relay() (bridge) prints them, so lossy conversions such as the tool_reference drop are invisible in the trial users run first.

Add `Format json.RawMessage` to outputConfig (Claude Code sends output_config.format {type:'json_schema', schema}) and forward it as `response_format: {type:'json_schema', json_schema:{name:'output', schema:<schema>}}` (llama.cpp, LM Studio, vLLM and OpenRouter accept it; Ollama takes `format`). At minimum, warn that it was dropped. Optionally, don't send reasoning_effort when thinking is absent (the title request).

When m.Reasoning != "", send it back: `reasoning_content` for llama.cpp, LM Studio and vLLM, `reasoning` for OpenRouter. At least do this for assistant turns after the last real user message (the current tool-call chain), so Qwen3.x and gpt-oss templates keep their interleaved reasoning and the runtime's cache matches what it generated.

Fix the cache-miss reasons. (1) Mark the end of the rendered tool definitions, not just the first <|end|>, so a divergence inside tools reads 'tool definitions changed (e.g. a deferred tool loaded via ToolSearch)'. Today #14 said 'a different conversation replaced this one' when WebFetch had been inserted mid-list. (2) Make resync insertion-aware: look for the old continuation a little further on in the new sequence. (3) When the divergence is inside the first user turn, label it 'new conversation; the shared system prompt and tools were reused' and don't count it as a miss. #13 said 'history was rewritten (e.g. compaction)' for a fresh session with a different prompt.

Put the simulated cache split (cache_read_input_tokens, with input_tokens excluding it) in message_start, not only message_delta. cyrlm knows it before the first token, and Claude Code uses these fields for context accounting.
Cosmetic: answer `HEAD /api/hello` with 200 (Claude Code's startup preconnect) instead of 404.

notes:
Both paths work end to end with Claude Code 2.1.319: greeting, Bash tool execution (tool.txt = tool-ok) and the follow-up after the tool result, in headless -p, stream-json and interactive TUI (tmux) modes.

cyrlm already handles the hardest new format change correctly: the mid-conversation role:'system' message is folded into the user turn as '[System note]', with one leading system message and a byte-stable prefix. It also handles the multi-block system prompt, adaptive thinking/effort, context_management, cache_control and thinking-signature round trips. CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS is honored (Claude Code debug log: effectiveWindow = value - 20000). The trial-log cache-miss explainer correctly flagged the attribution-header miss.

Main problems:
(1) The ToolSearch/deferred-tool flow sends the model an empty tool result, and that drop is silent in try/serve because warnings are only printed in bridge mode.
(2) The predictor's 33k base prompt is ~2.7x too big for this version; measured ~10.6k in -p and ~12k interactive.
(3) No CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS: Claude Code's 20k output reserve makes contexts under ~45k compact immediately, and 16k refuses to start.
(4) output_config.format and assistant reasoning are dropped on the way upstream.

Tool-search tradeoff for local runtimes: keeping it on (the default) halves the base prompt (10.6k vs 19.9k). But each deferred-tool load inserts a tool mid-list and forces a re-prefill on llama.cpp-style runtimes. The coding core (Bash, Read, Edit, Write) is always loaded, so keeping tool search on plus fixing tool_reference rendering seems best.

Sandbox caveats:
- The parent session exports many CLAUDE_*/ANTHROPIC_* variables (including ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://api.anthropic.com), so every harness run used `env -i` with HOME and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR inside the scratch dir. The real ~/.claude was never touched.
- The claude binary still read a container OAuth file (/home/claude/.claude/remote/.oauth_token), but ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN took precedence ('Bearer cyrlm' reached cyrlm). Vendor calls (Bootstrap, telemetry) failed fast with no effect on results.
- No flag containing 'dangerously' was used.

- claude-debugA.log, claude-debugB.log: Claude Code debug logs

instruction_problems: The snippet that try and bridge print (internal/harness/harness.go SetupFor, case "opencode") has no "limit": {"context": N, "output": M}, even though cyrlm knows the context (65536 in both runs). Without it opencode sends max_tokens: 32000 on every request; with limit.output 8192 or 16384 it sent exactly that, which I checked. It also does not know the window, so it cannot auto-compact before overflow. `cyrlm plan` (internal/setup/harness.go openCodeStep) already sets limit, so the two code paths disagree.
The bridge prints the trial wording: provider name "cyrlm (simulated local model)" and model name "<m> (simulated)". Two lines earlier the bridge itself says "Real local inference, no simulation."

Trial and bridge both use provider id "cyrlm" in the same file (opencode.json or ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json). Following the bridge instructions after a trial overwrites the trial provider's baseURL and models, so the two cannot live side by side. plan uses "cyrlm-<runtime>", a third naming scheme.

'Add to opencode.json (project) or ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json' plus 'Run in a new terminal window: opencode --model cyrlm/<m>' never says the project file only applies when opencode starts in that directory. It also makes the user edit a file, when opencode 1.19.5 accepts the whole config in OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT, so one command with no file edit works (verified).

The printed command starts the TUI only. Nothing mentions the headless form `opencode run --model cyrlm/<m> "task"`, or that `opencode run` blocks reading stdin when stdin is an open pipe (needs </dev/null in scripts; reproduced: it hangs until the pipe closes).

No mention that opencode contacts models.opencode.ai at startup. Offline or behind a firewall it logs 'Failed to fetch models.dev', and I saw two startup stalls in that state. OPENCODE_DISABLE_MODELS_FETCH=1 skips the fetch and costs nothing for a local provider.

With --background, the relayed child output still says 'Running (pid N). Stop with Ctrl-C, ...' right before '✓ Started in the background ... Stop: kill N'. Ctrl-C does not apply to a detached process.

Minor: the model name is right. 'cyrlm/qwen3.6:35b-a3b' with ':' and '.' parses fine in opencode (provider = text before the first '/'). No apiKey is needed for @ai-sdk/openai-compatible. "tool_call": true is valid.
request_shape_notes: Endpoint: only POST /v1/chat/completions, via @ai-sdk/openai-compatible. Each request has model, max_tokens (32000 when the config has no limit.output), messages, stream:true and stream_options:{include_usage:true}; requests that carry tools also have tools and tool_choice:'auto'. opencode never called GET /v1/models, /props or /api/*.

Each `opencode run` sends 3 requests: (1) a title-generation request with the same model (no tools; layout system + user + user, which cyrlm merges into one user message with a blank line before forwarding, harmless); (2) the main request with 1 system message (~9.8 KB with AGENTS.md included, ~2.1k tokens) and 10 function tools (bash, edit, glob, grep, read, skill, task, todowrite, webfetch, write; ~28 KB of JSON-schema parameters including a '$schema' key, no 'strict'); (3) the follow-up with assistant {content:'', tool_calls:[...]} and tool {tool_call_id, content:'(no output)'}.

Requests 1 and 2 are sent at the same time. On cyrlm's single-slot device the main request queued behind the title request ('waited 9.9 s for the device') and later evicted its cache ('cache miss at token 1 ... a different conversation used the only cache slot'). That models a real single-slot llama-server correctly. Setting "agent": {"title": {"disable": true}} removes the title request (verified: 2 requests instead of 3).

There was always exactly one system message, and it was first. Project AGENTS.md is merged into it. So the fake's strict Qwen-template check never fired, directly or through cyrlm, and opencode 1.19.5 does not need the bridge's reshaping.

The bash tool's arguments are {command, description} (optional timeout, workdir). The tool runs with permission 'allow' by default in `run` mode (log: evaluated permission=bash ... action=allow), so no --auto flag is needed.

Reasoning: cyrlm streams upstream reasoning_content deltas through and opencode shows them as reasoning parts. opencode does not send reasoning_content back on later assistant messages (cyrlm forwards content:null with tool_calls only).

cyrlm forwarded every field opencode sent (max_tokens, tools, tool_choice, stream_options). It only changes assistant content '' to null and merges consecutive user messages. No '!' warning lines in trial.log or bridge.log.

cyrlm's prompt-token counts in trial.log ('prompt 100' for a ~31 KB request, later 'prompt 6.9k', 'cached 119 of 120') come from scaling to the fake's hardcoded usage.prompt_tokens (100/120). This is a test artifact, not an opencode issue. Still, the calibrator accepts a 60x swing between the title and main requests without any sanity limit.

cyrlm's cache-miss explainer fired correctly when the working directory in opencode's system prompt changed between projects. Its suggested cause ('timestamp or attribution header') is generic, though.

OpenAI Compatible provider (User-Agent "ai-sdk-openai-compatible/3.0.67 ai-sdk-provider-utils/5.0.58 bun/1.4.2"): only POST /v1/chat/completions, with no /v1/models probe. Body: {model, messages, tools:[25], tool_choice:"auto", stream:true, stream_options:{include_usage:true}}. When contextWindow is set it adds max_tokens (32000 at a 5k-token prompt, computed as min(32000, window - input - reserve)). settings.maxTokens=8192 was not honored.

Message layout: turn 1 is [system, user]. Turn 2 is [system, user, assistant{content:null, tool_calls:[{id, type:function, function:{name, arguments}}]}, tool{name, tool_call_id, content: JSON string such as [{"query":"echo tool-ok > tool.txt","result":"","success":true}]}]. Exactly one system message, always first, so the strict Qwen-template 500 never triggered on either path.

Tools, all type function: read_files, search_codebase, run_commands {commands: [string], minItems 1}, fetch_web_content, editor, ask_question, spawn_agent, and 18 team_* tools. The shell tool is run_commands; the fake used {"commands":["echo tool-ok > tool.txt"]}. The system prompt is 4340 chars and the tool schemas are 18232 chars. cyrlm's tokenizer counts about 5.2k tokens, versus the 12000-token BasePromptTokens cyrlm assumes for Cline (that number fits the larger VS Code extension prompt, not CLI 3.x).

Approval: a positional prompt (`cline "task"`) runs in act mode with --auto-approve defaulting to true. run_commands ran with no prompt, so --yolo/-y was not needed or used. A run with no prompt opens the TUI and needs a TTY. --json gives NDJSON events (tool content_start/content_end, usage with cacheReadTokens, run_result finishReason).

The two AI SDK providers serialize empty-parameter tool schemas with different key order ("required":[] placement), and cyrlm keeps the client's raw schema JSON, so this is real client behavior, not a cyrlm bug.
